ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in $\triangle ABC$, points D and E are on sides AB and AC respectively, $AD:DB = 3:2$, $AE:EC = 1:2$. The line ED and the extension of CB intersect at point F. What is the value of $\frac{FB}{FC}$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Draw BG$\parallel$AC through point B, intersecting EF at point G,\\
since AD$\colon$DB = 3$\colon$2, AE$\colon$EC = 1$\colon$2,\\
thus AE = $\frac{1}{2}$EC,\\
thus $\triangle$BFG$\sim$$\triangle$CEF, $\triangle$BGD$\sim$$\triangle$AED,\\
thus $\frac{BG}{AE}=\frac{BD}{AD}=\frac{2}{3}$,\\
$\frac{BG}{EC}=\frac{FB}{FC}$,\\
thus $\frac{BG}{EC}=\frac{1}{3}$\\
thus $\frac{FB}{FC}=\boxed{\frac{1}{3}}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure is triangle ABC, with base BC horizontal, and point B is on the left side of C; BC is extended leftward to point F. Point D is located on side AB, point E is located on side AC, and F, D, E are on the same straight line, forming a secant line passing through two sides of the triangle and intersecting the extension of BC at F. Reasoning: Apply Menelaus' theorem to triangle ABC. The secant line F-D-E intersects AB at D, AC at E, and the extension of BC at F respectively, so according to length ratios it can be written as (AD/DB)(BF/FC)(CE/EA)=1. It is known that AD:DB=3:2, so AD/DB=3/2; it is known that AE:EC=1:2, so CE/EA=2. Substituting gives (3/2)(BF/FC)(2)=1, that is, 3·(BF/FC)=1, so BF/FC=1/3.
